decision: The frozen candidate accurately preserves a partial source-read lifecycle finding. Five terminated cutoff states and the two dated formal later events are supported; all earliest-end dates, the whole-order end, and the separate notice/records states remain unresolved.
rationale: The original establishes a Committee, its information functions, meetings/liaison, support, conditional termination, notice and records transfer. Seven textual units cover the complete substantive text; the three section 4 sentences remain distinct.

Section 4 makes actual completion of the Mediator duties under Public Law 93-531 section 1(a) the Committee termination condition. The negotiation time-limit reference in section 2(b) does not establish that occurrence. No completion date is inferred from a deadline or formal cleanup.

EO11853 expressly replaces section 2(a), bears April 17, 1975, and has no deferred commencement provision. Its complete replacement text is exact. The amendment date is a supported later event, but earlier own-terms cessation remains unproved and first_end correctly stays null.

EO12379 section 11 expressly revokes EO11829 as amended. The complete revoker bears August 17, 1982 and has no target savings or deferred effective clause. The candidate uses that date as formal revocation only. Its terminated cutoff findings do not claim that was the first cessation.

The original separately directs notice to the Chairman and transfer of any Committee records. Their occurrence is not established by either the amendment or revoker. Null notice/records states and null savings_residuals avoid a blanket completed-wind-down finding.

The actual statutory predicate and historical completion record are absent from the inspected packet; these are concrete limitations. Complete matched EO extracts suffice to support the limited formal amendment/revocation findings despite uninspected page images.

The ten claim-kit earlier actor/date bindings repeat EO12379 language and cannot establish those events. Rejecting these metadata bindings is not a claim to have read every earlier actor original or exhausted possible earlier effects.

Section 1. There is established the Hopi-Navajo Land Settlement 
Interagency Committee (hereinafter referred to as the Committee). The 
membership of the Committee shall consist of the Secretary of the Interior,

culture, the Secretary of Commerce, the Secretary of Labor, the Secre­
tary of Health, Education, and Welfare, and the Secretary of Housing 
and Urban Development.

By virtue of the authority vested in me by Section 1(c)(2)  of the 
Act to provide for final settlement of the conflicting rights and interests 
of the Hopi and Navajo Tribes concerning lands within the reservation 
established by the Executive order of December 16, 1882, and lands 
within the reservation created by the Act of June 14, 1934, and for 
other purposes (Public Law 93— 531, approved December 22, 1974, 
hereinafter referred to as the A ct), and as President of the United States 
of America, Section 2(a)  of Executive Order No. 11829 of January 6, 
1975, is hereby amended to read as follows:
“ Sec. 2. Functions of the Committee, (a.)  The Committee shall, to 
the extent permitted by law, and as provided by Section 1(c)(2)  of the 
Act, develop relevant information for and respond to the requests of the 
Mediator who shall be appointed by the Director of the Federal Media­
tion and Conciliation Service pursuant to Section 1(a)  of the Act, in 
order to facilitate the expeditious and orderly compilation and develop­
ment of factual information relevant to the negotiation process estab­
lished by the Act.”

necessity_qualifications: The image limitation is retained as a disclosure of what was inspected, not treated as an independent legal blocker for these complete, unambiguous official EO extracts with matching recorded fixity. No page-image or newly retained-PDF check is certified.

The express records-transfer command creates a concrete residual inquiry. The candidate reference to any independent continuing records obligations records non-establishment; this review does not impose speculative, unbounded proof of the absence of every possible independent records duty.

The actual text of the controlling statute and historical completion determination are material to selecting the earliest termination date. Reading the statute alone would not establish the historical occurrence.
retained_material_gaps_as_written: Actual original, amending and revoking PDF page images were not present at the cited cache locations and were not inspected. GPO fixity rows match the recorded PDF hashes; exact held OCR is not an authenticated page transcription.

EO 11829 section 4 ties termination to completion of the Mediator duties as determined under Public Law 93-531 section 1(a). The controlling statute and evidence of actual completion are not held in the inspected packet/search results. No original clause first-end or whole_order_end date is asserted.

EO 11853 replaced section 2(a) on April 17, 1975 using immediate amendment wording. Earlier cessation under section 4 and the statute has not been ruled out; the amendment is a later event only, with the complete replacement text retained in its source.

Section 4 separately requires the Mediator to advise the Chairman when duties cease and directs transfer of Committee records to the Secretary of the Interior. Actual notice, transfer, and any independent continuing records obligations have not been established; these commands cannot be dismissed with committee termination.

The held machine searches do not determine the historical triggering occurrence or records transfer. U.S. Code coverage stops at 2026-10-09, leaving cutoff coverage through 2026-10-14 unclosed. later_source_search remains empty.

The claim-kit chain misattributes EO 12379 language to ten other orders and their dates. These associations are rejected from the full actor text; target EDGES rows identify only EO 11853 and EO 12379. No exhaustive negative earlier-history finding is made.
